section_summary: This section documents Japan’s April 1947 elections through occupation reports, analyses of the revised electoral system, interviews with party figures, Soviet press commentary, election results and British editorials. It also includes a handbook for military government election observers and a brief exchange about research sources.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on House of Representatives election-law amendments
subfiles.to: War Department for Joint Chiefs of Staff and General McCoy
subfiles.about: Reports the Diet’s extension of revised electoral rules to the House of Representatives.
subfiles.summary: The amendments broaden voting eligibility, create 117 districts returning 466 members, transfer election supervision to committees, raise deposits and penalties, adopt a single ballot, and restrict use of children in campaigns.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram summarizing Izvestia criticism of Japanese electoral law
subfiles.about: Relays an Izvestia article portraying Yoshida’s electoral changes as a return to prewar politics.
subfiles.summary: The article links the Liberal Party and revised electoral law to General Tanaka’s era, criticizes the occupation’s response, and argues that Yoshida cannot democratize Japan.

subfiles.title: File note on electoral-system study
subfiles.about: Recommends reading the enclosed study of the new electoral system.
subfiles.summary: Calls the study of the new system’s merits or demerits worth reading in full.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 998 transmitting analysis of Yoshida’s electoral system
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Roest’s memorandum on the proposed electoral system.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the March 17 Government Section memorandum on Yoshida’s proposal.

subfiles.title: The Merits of the Electoral System Proposed by Mr. Yoshida
subfiles.about: Assesses smaller districts and single-vote elections proposed by Yoshida.
subfiles.summary: Roest argues that the proposal would favor entrenched party machines, narrow voters’ choices, weaken minority parties and sharply reduce women’s chances of election.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1000 transmitting Nozaka interview
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum on Nozaka’s views and Communist election plans.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the March 10 interview memorandum concerning Sanzō Nozaka.

subfiles.title: Interview with Nozaka
subfiles.about: Records Nozaka’s political program and plans for the April elections.
subfiles.summary: Nozaka describes a program of purges, administrative reform, land reform and nationalization, alongside longer-term socialist goals. He discusses cooperation and differences with Socialists, parliamentary and mass action, and relations with Soviet Communists. He also gives campaign funding, candidate numbers and expected regional gains.

subfiles.title: File note on Narahashi interview
subfiles.about: Comments on the enclosed Narahashi interview and pending purge appeals.
subfiles.summary: Notes the interview’s continuing interest and the status of several purge appeals.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1001 transmitting Narahashi interview
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum on Narahashi’s plan to reorganize the Progressive Party.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the March 31 interview memorandum on creation of the Democratic Party.

subfiles.title: Interview with Narahashi Wataru
subfiles.about: Records Narahashi’s plans for a new Democratic Party and his political ambitions.
subfiles.summary: Narahashi proposes turning the Progressive Party into a centrist Democratic Party with broader labor support and elected officers. He discusses Ashida, Inukai, Shidehara, possible party presidents and post-election coalitions. Roest judges him energetic and influential but potentially overconfident.

subfiles.title: File note on local-election interview
subfiles.about: Identifies the enclosed March interview about Tokyo-area local elections.
subfiles.summary: Describes the enclosed interview as concerning prospects for Tokyo-area local elections.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1004 transmitting local-election interview
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits an interview on local and Diet elections in Tokyo Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the March 13 memorandum concerning Tokyo election prospects.

subfiles.title: Interview with Okubo Tomejiro
subfiles.from: P. K. Roest; prepared by John K. McLean
subfiles.about: Records a Liberal Party campaign manager’s assessment of Tokyo elections.
subfiles.summary: Ōkubo describes proposed Liberal–Progressive cooperation, support for Governor Yasui, candidate and seat expectations, campaign funds, strong wards and party policy. The memorandum notes the importance of personalities and financing in closely contested Tokyo races.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram summarizing Pravda on Japanese elections
subfiles.about: Relays Pravda’s interpretation of Japan’s April parliamentary elections.
subfiles.summary: Pravda charges that conservative parties, electoral changes, delayed purges and American policy favored Japanese reaction. It describes Communist and Socialist organizing, alleges intimidation, and urges a united democratic front.

subfiles.title: Secretariat cover note for Japanese election review
subfiles.about: Submits Vincent’s review of the elections for information.
subfiles.summary: Notes that Acheson has seen the attached review.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Elections
subfiles.about: Reviews election results and their implications for Japan’s next government.
subfiles.summary: Allison reports Socialist gains, weak Communist results and the Democrats’ pivotal role in cabinet formation.

subfiles.title: London despatch transmitting British editorials
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, U.S. Embassy London
subfiles.about: Transmits Times and Manchester Guardian editorials on the Japanese elections.
subfiles.summary: Forwards contrasting British newspaper assessments of the election.

subfiles.title: Democracy in Japan
subfiles.about: Editorial assesses conservative electoral victories and Japan’s democratic prospects.
subfiles.summary: The Times expresses concern about low turnout, conservative strength and resistance to occupation reforms. It urges renewed trade and commercial links while recognizing Japan’s uncertainty before a peace settlement.

subfiles.title: Japan at the Polls
subfiles.about: Editorial considers Socialist gains and Japan’s economic difficulties.
subfiles.summary: The Guardian says conservatives remain in power and calls for a stronger response to inflation and unrest.

subfiles.title: Democracy in Japan, second clipping copy
subfiles.about: Second copy of The Times editorial on the Japanese elections.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the editorial’s concern about conservative victories, occupation reform and the need to restore external trade.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file note on elections
subfiles.about: Partly illegible note refers to elections and the Government Section.
subfiles.summary: Brief, largely illegible note mentions elections and the Government Section.

subfiles.title: Turner letter on thesis research
subfiles.about: Clarifies Turner’s thesis topic concerning Japanese political liberalism.
subfiles.summary: Turner responds to Appleton’s request for more detail about his research topic.

subfiles.title: Appleton reply on English-language research sources
subfiles.about: Suggests English-language newspapers for Turner’s thesis research.
subfiles.summary: Appleton recommends several English-language Japanese newspapers and notes the limited material available in English.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1037 transmitting Diet elections handbook
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits the Government Section handbook used by election observers.
subfiles.summary: Forwards three copies of the April 1947 election handbook.

subfiles.title: Hand Book and Laws for Japanese Diet Elections, April 1947
subfiles.from: Government Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Military government officers and election teams
subfiles.about: Instructs occupation observers on fair elections and explains national election procedures.
subfiles.summary: The opening chapter directs observers to watch for intimidation, fraud, unlawful exclusions, excessive spending and official favoritism while maintaining strict impartiality and referring complaints to Japanese authorities. The next chapter outlines Diet seats, voter and candidate qualifications, campaign restrictions, election committees, polling, ballot counting and tabulation. The handbook continues beyond page 115.
